title: Recording Custodial Interrogations
key_points: Custodial interrogations in a place of detention must be electronically recorded when the person is suspected of murder, manslaughter, kidnapping, robbery, aggravated sexual assault, sexual assault and other listed serious crimes.
Exceptions exist (for example, the suspect refuses to be recorded, or the statement is spontaneous), and they must be documented.
If an unexcused recording is missing, the court may exclude the statement or give the jury a cautionary instruction.
